concept: Unsloth server-side tools versus agent passthrough
summary: Unsloth's server-side tools are Python execution, web search and a terminal (bash) tool, and results stream back as `tool_result` events.

facts.text: Unsloth's server-side tools are Python execution, web search and a terminal (bash) tool, and results stream back as `tool_result` events.
A request opts in with `enable_tools: true` and `enabled_tools: ["python", "web_search", "terminal"]` (plus an optional `session_id`) on either the OpenAI-style or Anthropic-style endpoint.
The API page's troubleshooting says that for built-in tools both `enable_tools: true` and an `enabled_tools` list are required, or the tools do not run.
The stated reason for the network default is that a leaked API key on a network-exposed server would mean arbitrary code execution on the host.

With server-side tools off, the model still sees client-side tools sent in `tools` and `tool_choice` in native OpenAI or Anthropic form, and Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Continue and Cline are listed as working with them.

Unsloth's Codex guide gives the same instruction as the Claude Code guide: add `--disable-tools` when driving an external coding agent, so the agent's own tools are forwarded and returned as tool calls instead of Unsloth running built-in tools.

The Codex guide shows `-c 131072` (with `--reasoning on`) as the way to set the context window, and a separate coding-agent command `unsloth run --model ... --disable-tools -p 8888`; with no flags Unsloth picks recommended context length and temperature.
The Codex guide says Unsloth's self-healing tool calling is on by default and helps when tool calling is unreliable.
The Claude Code guide's `--disable-tools` command line is `unsloth run --model ... --disable-tools --reasoning off -p 8888` for a coding agent.
Inferred: `--disable-tools` is the only control the docs document for agent passthrough, so a Mac user binding Studio to loopback for Claude Code should always pass it.
Inferred: binding to `0.0.0.0` makes passthrough the default, so a LAN-served Studio needs no extra flag for Claude Code but loses the built-in tools.
